questions.question:
Select the correct law for the following statement.

During a chemical reaction mass is neither created nor destroyed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Law of conservation of mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Law of Conservation of Mass states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
• This law was formulated by Antoine Lavoisier in 1789.
 
• It is a fundamental principle of classical physics and chemistry.
 
• During a chemical reaction, the total mass of the reactants is equal to the total mass of the products.
 
• This law is essential for balancing chemical equations and understanding stoichiometry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Thermodynamics**

 
 
• It comprises four laws that describe the relationships between heat, work, temperature, and energy.
 
• These laws are fundamental for understanding the physical properties of matter and the behavior of energy in different systems.
 
 
 
• **Henry's Law**
 
 
• This law states that the amount of gas that dissolves in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of that gas above the liquid.
 
• It is used in various applications, including calculating the solubility of gases in liquids under different conditions.
 
 
 
• **Charles' Law**
 
 
• This law states that the volume of a gas is directly proportional to its temperature, provided the pressure remains constant.
 
• It is a part of the ideal gas law and is essential for understanding the behavior of gases under varying temperature conditions.

questions.question: The relation between thrust (T), pressure (P) and area (A) of an object in a given medium is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: T = P x A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Thrust (T) is a force exerted by the pressure (P) acting over a specific area (A).
 
• The formula for thrust is given by the product of pressure and area: T = P x A.
 
• This relationship indicates that thrust increases with an increase in either pressure or area.
 
• Pressure is defined as the force per unit area, and when multiplied by area, it gives the total force or thrust.
 
• Understanding this relationship is crucial in fields such as fluid dynamics and aerodynamics, where pressure and thrust play a significant role.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fluid Dynamics**

 
 
• It is the study of the movement of liquids and gases and their interactions with solid boundaries.
 
• Understanding the principles of fluid dynamics is essential for designing efficient systems in engineering and natural sciences.
 
 
 
• **Aerodynamics**
 
 
• Aerodynamics is the study of the behavior of air as it interacts with solid objects, such as an aircraft wing.
 
• It involves the application of fluid dynamics principles to understand and predict the forces and moments acting on bodies in motion through the air.
 
 
 
• **Pressure Measurement**
 
 
• Pressure is measured using instruments like manometers, barometers, and pressure transducers.
 
• Accurate measurement of pressure is vital in various industrial and scientific applications to ensure system efficiency and safety.

questions.question: Which of the following is obtained upon heating ferrous sulphate?

options.text: Ferric oxide, sulphur dioxide and sulphur trioxide

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ferric oxide, sulphur dioxide and sulphur trioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Upon heating, ferrous sulphate decomposes to form ferric oxide, sulphur dioxide, and sulphur trioxide.
 
• The chemical reaction involved is: 2 FeSO₄ (s) → Fe₂O₃ (s) + SO₂ (g) + SO₃ (g).
 
• This is an example of a thermal decomposition reaction where a compound breaks down into simpler substances when heated.
 
• Ferric oxide is a solid, while sulphur dioxide and sulphur trioxide are gases.
 
• Sulphur dioxide and sulphur trioxide are acidic oxides that can contribute to acid rain when released into the atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thermal Decomposition**

 
 
• It is a chemical reaction where a chemical compound breaks down into simpler substances when heated.
 
• Thermal decomposition reactions are usually endothermic, meaning they absorb heat.
 
 
 
• **Sulphur Dioxide (SO₂)**
 
 
• It is a colorless gas with a pungent odor, used in the production of sulfuric acid and as a preservative.
 
• SO₂ can cause respiratory problems and is a major air pollutant.
 
 
 
• **Sulphur Trioxide (SO₃)**
 
 
• It is a highly reactive substance used in the production of sulfuric acid.
 
• SO₃ can form a mist in the air and contribute to environmental pollution.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about sodium carbonate?

options.text: Sodium carbonate is used in glass, soap and paper industries.
Sodium carbonate is used in the manufacture of sodium compounds, such as borax.
Sodium carbonate is used to neutralise excess acid in the stomach.
Sodium carbonate can be used as a cleaning agent for domestic purposes.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sodium carbonate(Na₂Co₃), also known as soda ash or washing soda, is widely used in the glass, soap, and paper industries.
 
• It is utilized in the manufacture of various sodium compounds, such as borax.
 
• Sodium carbonate is not typically used to neutralize excess acid in the stomach; this role is usually fulfilled by sodium bicarbonate.
 
• It can be used as a cleaning agent for domestic purposes, such as removing grease and oil stains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sodium Bicarbonate**

 
 
• Commonly known as baking soda, it is used to neutralize stomach acid and relieve heartburn and indigestion.
 
• It is also used in baking as a leavening agent.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Hydroxide**
 
 
• Also known as caustic soda, it is used in the manufacture of soaps, paper, and various chemicals.
 
• It is a strong base and can cause severe chemical burns.
 
 
 
• **Calcium Carbonate**
 
 
• This compound is used as a dietary calcium supplement and as an antacid to relieve heartburn and indigestion.
 
• It is also used in the construction industry as a building material and in the production of lime and cement.

questions.question: In Fleming's left hand rule, which physical quantity is represented by the middle finger?

options.text: Direction of the motion of conductor

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Direction of electric current**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fleming's left-hand rule is used to determine the direction of force experienced by a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
 
• According to Fleming's left-hand rule, the thumb represents the direction of the force or motion.
 
• The first finger (index finger) represents the direction of the magnetic field.
 
• The middle finger represents the direction of the electric current.
 
• This rule is particularly useful in electric motors to find the direction of force acting on the armature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fleming's Right-Hand Rule**

 
 
• This rule is used to determine the direction of induced current when a conductor moves in a magnetic field.
 
• According to this rule, the thumb points in the direction of motion of the conductor, the first finger in the direction of the magnetic field, and the middle finger gives the direction of the induced current.
 
 
 
• **Electric Motors**
 
 
• Electric motors work on the principle of electromagnetic induction, which involves the interaction of magnetic fields and electric currents to produce motion.
 
• Fleming's left-hand rule helps in understanding the operation of electric motors by determining the direction of force on the motor's armature.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic Induction**
 
 
• This is the process of generating electric current in a conductor by changing the magnetic field around it.
 
• Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction describe how a change in magnetic field can induce an electromotive force (EMF) in a conductor.

questions.question: Which cell organelle serves as a channel for transport of material between various regions of cytoplasm?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Endoplasmic reticulum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) serves as a **channel for the transport of materials** between various regions of the cytoplasm.
 
• The ER is an extensive network of membranes found throughout the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells.
 
• It is divided into two regions: the **rough ER** (which has ribosomes attached to its surface) and the **smooth ER** (which lacks ribosomes).
 
• The rough ER is primarily involved in the synthesis and processing of proteins, while the smooth ER is involved in lipid synthesis and detoxification.
 
• The ER is crucial for the **transport and modification of proteins** that are either secreted by the cell or incorporated into the cell membrane.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondria**

 
 
• Known as the powerhouses of the cell, they generate most of the cell's supply of ATP, used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• They have a double-membrane structure and their own DNA and ribosomes.
 
 
 
• **Lysosomes**
 
 
• These membrane-bound organelles contain enzymes responsible for breaking down waste materials and cellular debris.
 
• Referred to as the "digestive system" of the cell, they help degrade macromolecules.
 
 
 
• **Chloroplast**
 
 
• These organelles are found in plant cells and eukaryotic algae and conduct photosynthesis.
 
• They capture light energy and convert it into chemical energy in the form of glucose through photosynthesis.

questions.question: If a person can see far objects distinctly but cannot see nearby objects clearly, then this eye defect can be corrected by using ______.

options.text: a concave lens of suitable power
a convex lens of suitable power

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a convex lens of suitable power**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The condition where a person can see distant objects clearly but has difficulty seeing nearby objects is called **hypermetropia** or farsightedness.
 
• Hypermetropia occurs when the eyeball is too short or the lens is not curved enough, causing light to focus behind the retina.
 
• This condition can be corrected by using a **convex lens** of suitable power.
 
• A convex lens converges light rays before they enter the eye, thus allowing the light to focus directly on the retina.
 
• Using a convex lens helps in adjusting the focal length so that nearby objects can be seen clearly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Myopia**

 
 
• Myopia, or nearsightedness, is a condition where a person can see nearby objects clearly but has difficulty seeing distant objects.
 
• It is usually corrected using concave lenses, which diverge light rays before they enter the eye.
 
 
 
• **Astigmatism**
 
 
• Astigmatism is a common vision condition caused by an irregularly shaped cornea or lens.
 
• It can cause blurred or distorted vision at all distances and is usually corrected with cylindrical lenses.
 
 
 
• **Presbyopia**
 
 
• Presbyopia is an age-related condition where the eye's lens loses its flexibility, making it difficult to focus on close objects.
 
• This condition can be corrected using bifocal or progressive lenses that have different sections for distance and near vision.

questions.concept: Basic Concepts of Chemistry, Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.question: Which of the following metals are mixed with iron to get stainless steel?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**nickel and chromium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Stainless steel is primarily made by mixing iron with chromium and nickel to enhance its properties.
 
• Chromium is added to stainless steel to improve its corrosion resistance and to create a passive layer that prevents rust.
 
• Nickel is added to increase the toughness and strength of stainless steel, especially at low temperatures.
 
• Stainless steel is widely used in various applications due to its durability, resistance to corrosion, and aesthetic appearance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Stainless Steel**

 
 
• There are different types of stainless steel, including austenitic, ferritic, martensitic, and duplex, each with unique properties and applications.
 
• Austenitic stainless steel is the most common type, known for its excellent corrosion resistance and formability.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Stainless Steel**
 
 
• Stainless steel is used in a wide range of industries, including construction, automotive, medical, and food processing.
 
• Its resistance to corrosion makes it ideal for kitchen appliances, cutlery, and surgical instruments.
 
 
 
• **Maintenance of Stainless Steel**
 
 
• Regular cleaning and maintenance can help preserve the appearance and longevity of stainless steel products.
 
• Using mild detergents and avoiding abrasive cleaners will prevent damage to the passive layer of stainless steel.

questions.concept: Chemistry in Everyday Life, States of Matter
questions.question: Solid CO₂ gets converted directly into the gaseous state upon decreasing the pressure to ________.

options.text: 2 atmosphere, without coming to the liquid state
1 atmosphere, without coming to the liquid state
3 atmosphere, without coming to the liquid state
4 atmosphere, without coming to the liquid state

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 atmosphere, without coming to the liquid state**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Solid carbon dioxide (CO₂) is commonly known as dry ice.
 
• Dry ice sublimates, meaning it changes directly from a solid to a gas without passing through the liquid state.
 
• This sublimation occurs at atmospheric pressure, which is approximately 1 atmosphere.
 
• The temperature at which dry ice sublimates is -78.5 degrees Celsius.
 
• Decreasing the pressure around dry ice further enhances the sublimation process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uses of Dry Ice**

 
 
• Dry ice is used for refrigeration, especially for shipping perishable goods.
 
• It is also used in fog machines to create dense, low-lying fog effects.
 
 
 
• **Safety Precautions**
 
 
• Handling dry ice requires protective gloves, as it can cause severe frostbite.
 
• It should be used in well-ventilated areas to prevent the buildup of CO2 gas, which can be dangerous.
 
 
 
• **Storage and Handling**
 
 
• Dry ice should be stored in insulated containers to slow down the sublimation process.
 
• It should never be stored in airtight containers, as the pressure buildup from sublimating CO2 can cause the container to burst.

questions.question: Where does the centre of curvature of a concave mirror lie?

options.text: At the centre of the mirror
At the edge of the mirror

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In front of the mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The centre of curvature of a concave mirror is the point on the principal axis at which the reflected rays converge.
 
• This point lies at a distance equal to the radius of curvature from the mirror's surface.
 
• It is denoted by the letter 'C' in ray diagrams.
 
• Since the concave mirror converges light, the centre of curvature is located in front of the mirror.
 
• It is a real point and can be used to determine the focal length of the mirror, which is half the radius of curvature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirrors**

 
 
• These are mirrors with a surface that curves inward like a cave, often used in telescopes and shaving mirrors.
 
• They form real, inverted images when the object is placed beyond the focal point.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirrors**
 
 
• These mirrors have a surface that curves outward, used in vehicle side mirrors for a wider field of view.
 
• They always form virtual, erect, and diminished images regardless of the object's position.
 
 
 
• **Focal Point**
 
 
• The focal point of a concave mirror is the point where parallel rays converge after reflecting off the mirror.
 
• It is located halfway between the mirror's surface and its centre of curvature.

questions.question: Blood brings carbon dioxide from the rest of the body for release into the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**alveoli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Alveoli are tiny air sacs in the lungs where the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide takes place.
 
• They are located at the end of the respiratory tree and are the primary sites for gas exchange in the respiratory system.
 
• The walls of alveoli are extremely thin, allowing for efficient diffusion of gases between the air and the blood.
 
• Alveoli are surrounded by a network of capillaries, which facilitate the transfer of oxygen into the blood and carbon dioxide out of the blood.
 
• Each lung contains millions of alveoli, providing a large surface area for gas exchange to meet the body's needs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bronchi**

 
 
• The bronchi are the main passageways that lead from the trachea to the lungs and branch into smaller tubes called bronchioles.
 
• They help carry air to and from the alveoli.
 
 
 
• **Diaphragm**
 
 
• The diaphragm is a dome-shaped muscle located below the lungs that plays a crucial role in breathing.
 
• When the diaphragm contracts, it creates a vacuum that allows air to enter the lungs.
 
 
 
• **Capillaries**
 
 
• Capillaries are small blood vessels where the exchange of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nutrients, and waste products occurs between the blood and tissues.
 
• They are essential for supplying oxygen and nutrients to tissues and removing waste products.

questions.question: Which physical quantity represents the rate at which electric energy is dissipated or consumed in an electric circuit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electric Power**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Electric power** is the rate at which **electric energy** is dissipated or consumed in an electric circuit.
 
• The formula to calculate electric power is **P = VI**, where **P** represents power, **V** is the potential difference, and **I** is the current.</l

questions.question: Which of the following organisms reproduces by budding?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hydra is a genus of small, fresh-water organisms that belong to the phylum Cnidaria.
 
• Reproduction in Hydra occurs through a process called budding, where a new individual develops from an outgrowth or bud due to cell division at one particular site.
 
• The bud initially remains attached to the parent organism and then detaches to become an independent organism.
 
• Budding is an asexual mode of reproduction, allowing for rapid population growth under favorable conditions.
 
• Hydra can also reproduce sexually, but budding is the most common and frequent mode of reproduction in these organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Earthworm**

 
 
• Earthworms reproduce sexually through a process called copulation, where two worms exchange sperm.
 
• They are hermaphrodites, meaning each individual possesses both male and female reproductive organs.
 
 
 
• **Frog**
 
 
• Frogs reproduce sexually with external fertilization, where the female lays eggs and the male fertilizes them outside her body.
 
• Frogs undergo a complex life cycle including egg, tadpole, and adult stages.
 
 
 
• **Cockroach**
 
 
• Cockroaches reproduce sexually with internal fertilization, where the male deposits sperm inside the female's body.
 
• They lay eggs in protective cases called oothecae, which hatch into nymphs that undergo several molts before becoming adults.

questions.question: A moving body covers 10 m distance along a straight path in each second. The body is under which type of motion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uniform motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• In uniform motion, a body covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.
 
• The velocity of the body remains constant throughout the motion.
 
• There is no acceleration in uniform motion as the speed does not change.
 
• Examples of uniform motion include a car moving at a constant speed on a straight road.</li

questions.question: A solution contains 40 ml of acid in 120 ml of water. Calculate the concentration in terms of volume by volume percentage of the solution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.25**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Volume by volume percentage is calculated using the formula: frac{{Volume of solute}}{{Total volume of solution}} times 100.
 
• Here, the volume of the solute (acid) is 40 ml.
 
• The total volume of the solution is the sum of the volume of the solute and the solvent: 40 {ml} + 120 {ml} = 160 {ml}.
 
• Using the formula: frac{40 {ml}}{160 {ml}} times 100 = 25\%.
 
• The concentration in terms of volume by volume percentage of the solution is 0.25 or 25%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concentration units**

 
 
• Concentration can be expressed in various units such as molarity, molality, mass by volume percentage, and volume by volume percentage.
 
 
 
• **Applications of concentration**
 
 
• Concentration is a critical factor in chemical reactions, pharmaceuticals, and solutions in various industries.
 
 
 
• **Importance of accurate measurements**
 
 
• Accurate measurements of solute and solvent volumes are essential for precise concentration calculations.

questions.question: Reflex arcs are formed in which part of the nervous system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Spinal cord**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Reflex arcs are formed in the **spinal cord**, which is a part of the central nervous system.
 
• They are responsible for involuntary and nearly instantaneous movements in response to a stimulus.
 
• A reflex arc typically involves a sensory neuron, an interneuron, and a motor neuron, which facilitate the immediate reaction.
 
• The spinal cord acts as an intermediary, processing the reflex without involving the brain, thus saving time.
 
• Reflex actions help protect the body from harm, such as quickly withdrawing a hand from a hot surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Medulla**

 
 
• It is part of the brainstem that controls autonomic functions like breathing and heart rate.
 
• The medulla is not involved in the formation of reflex arcs but is critical for vital life functions.
 
 
 
• **Forebrain**
 
 
• This region includes structures such as the cerebrum and thalamus, involved in complex behaviors and cognitive functions.
 
• It does not play a direct role in reflex arcs.
 
 
 
• **Cerebellum**
 
 
• The cerebellum is responsible for coordinating voluntary movements and maintaining balance and posture.
 
• While important for motor control, it is not directly involved in reflex arcs.

questions.question: A car moves with a uniform velocity (v) in a particular direction for a distance (s) under the action of a force (F) acting in the same direction. The work done by the force will be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Work done (W) by a force (F) is calculated using the formula: **W = F × s**, where s is the displacement.
 
• In this problem, the force (F) and displacement (s) are in the same direction.
 
• Hence, the work done is positive and is given by the product of the force and displacement.
 
• Uniform velocity (v) indicates that the force is applied uniformly over the distance.
 
• Therefore, the correct option for the work done by the force is **Fs** (Option 2).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Force and Work**

 
 
• Force is a vector quantity that causes an object to move or change its motion.
 
• Work is a scalar quantity and is the measure of energy transfer when a force moves an object over a distance.
 
 
 
• **Energy**
 
 
• Energy is the capacity to do work and is measured in joules (J).
 
• Work and energy are closely related; the work done on an object transfers energy to the object.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy**
 
 
• An object moving with velocity (v) has kinetic energy given by the formula: KE = 0.5 × m × v².
 
• The work done by a force can change the kinetic energy of an object.

questions.question: Variegated leaves are found in which of the following plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Croton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Variegated leaves are leaves that have multiple colors, often displaying patterns of green with white, yellow, or other colors.
 
• Croton plants are known for their vibrant, multi-colored leaves which make them popular as ornamental plants.
 
• The variegation in Croton leaves is due to the presence of different pigments such as chlorophyll, carotenoids, and anthocyanins.
 
• Variegated leaves can sometimes have reduced chlorophyll, leading to sections of the leaf that are less green or even white.
 
• Variegation can occur naturally or be induced through selective breeding and genetic manipulation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Banana Plant**

 
 
• Banana plants typically have large, green leaves without variegation.
 
• They are primarily known for their fruit rather than their foliage.
 
 
 
• **Neem Plant**
 
 
• Neem leaves are usually green and do not exhibit variegation.
 
• Neem is valued for its medicinal properties.
 
 
 
• **Rose Plant**
 
 
• Rose leaves are typically green and do not exhibit variegation.
 
• Roses are primarily cultivated for their flowers.

questions.question: Burning of naphthalene on a spatula gives a ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**yellow flame**__.

**Note:** We have provided the answer as per the official answer key. Naphthalene is an unsaturated compound and hence, it burns with a yellow flame with release of black smoke (sooty flame). Thus, both Option 3 and Option 4 can be correct but Option 3 is the right answer as per the official answer key.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Naphthalene, when burned, produces a yellow flame.
 
• This yellow flame is due to the incomplete combustion of naphthalene.
 
• Incomplete combustion occurs because naphthalene is a hydrocarbon and has a high carbon content.
 
• The yellow color in the flame is typically due to the presence of carbon particles (soot) that are heated to incandescence.
 
• Naphthalene combustion often produces a noticeable amount of soot and smoke.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrocarbons**

 
 
• Hydrocarbons are organic compounds consisting entirely of hydrogen and carbon atoms.
 
• They can be found in various forms such as alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes.
 
• Common hydrocarbons include methane, ethane, propane, and butane.
 
 
 
• **Combustion**
 
 
• Combustion is a chemical reaction that occurs between a fuel and an oxidizing agent, producing heat and light.
 
• Complete combustion produces carbon dioxide and water, while incomplete combustion can produce carbon monoxide and soot.
 
 
 
• **Soot**
 
 
• Soot is a black powdery or flaky substance consisting largely of amorphous carbon, produced by the incomplete burning of organic matter.
 
• Soot can have various health impacts and contribute to air pollution.

questions.question: Which elements of xylem tissue form interconnected water-conducting channels?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vessels and Tracheids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Xylem is a type of vascular tissue in plants responsible for the conduction of water and nutrients from the roots to the rest of the plant.
 
• Vessels and tracheids are the primary water-conducting elements in the xylem tissue.
 
• Vessels are long tubes formed by the end-to-end connection of vessel elements, allowing efficient water transport.
 
• Tracheids are elongated cells with tapered ends that overlap each other, facilitating water movement through their pits.
 
• Both vessels and tracheids have thick, lignified walls that provide structural support to the plant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8bcced9228da63df94044622ceab189bf61874ec72cd8b35477d549969e0e950.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Xylem Fibers**

 
 
• These are supportive fibers present in the xylem that provide mechanical strength to the plant.
 
• They are not involved in water conduction.
 
 
 
• **Phloem**
 
 
• It is another type of vascular tissue responsible for the transport of nutrients, particularly sugars, from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
• Phloem consists of sieve tube elements, companion cells, phloem fibers, and phloem parenchyma.
 
 
 
• **Plant Roots**
 
 
• Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil and transport them to the xylem.
 
• They also anchor the plant and store nutrients.
